blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Super Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) further weakened on Thursday morning, said the state weather bureau, as it continued to move northwestward over the Philippine Sea. According to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) in its latest typhoon bulletin, Rosal was last spotted 400 kilometers (km) east of Basco, Batanes as of 11 a.m. READ: Palace: Collect rainwater from Super Typhoon Rosal As of writing, Rosal now carries maximum sustained wind speeds of 185 km per hour (kph) and gustiness of up to 230 kph (from Thursday early morning’s 195 kph and 240 kph, respectively).
